name: Tin bronze CuSn10, the museum's one bronze
summary: A lead-free tin bronze of about 90 parts copper to 10 parts tin (EN 1982 CuSn10-C, CC480K; UNS C90700; BS 1400 CT1). It is the classical casting bronze: golden when bright, it fills fine detail, it takes the founder's hot patinas, and it is made both as castings and as continuously cast bar, so every bronze piece in the museum (the sun clock's inlaid lines, numerals and letters, the doorway threshold strips, the well-collar rings, the rails) can be the one alloy. Its workings are cast.bronze, brushed and patinated; brass is its declared accent.

chosenBecause.text: It is the classical casting bronze: 'classic bronze', about 10 % tin, was used in casting; 'mild bronze', about 6 % tin, was hammered.
Art foundries cast statuary in tin bronze; a typical composition is about 90 % copper and 10 % tin.
chosenBecause.source: Kunstguss Lauchhammer (art foundry), 'Bronze' ('For the production of bronze sculptures, we usually use our own tin bronze recipes'), https://lauchhammer.com/en/worth-knowing/bronze

chosenBecause.text: Its colour is the bronze colour: tin bronzes of 5-12 % Sn are orange-brown to yellow-golden and 'at 10 % when polished distinctly golden (typical bronze color)', with good casting qualities. The measured yellowness reaches its maximum between 11 and 13 % Sn.
chosenBecause.source: M. Moedlinger, M. H. G. Kuijpers, D. Braekmans, D. Berger, 'Quantitative comparisons of the color of CuAs, CuSn, CuNi, and CuSb alloys', J. Archaeol. Sci. 88 (2017) 14-23, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2017.09.001, Table 2 (after Kuijpers 2014) and Discussion; accepted manuscript https://scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl/access/item:2949755/download

chosenBecause.text: Bronze expands slightly just before it sets, filling the finest detail of a mould, then shrinks a little on cooling.

One alloy for every product form: EN 1982 CuSn10-C is supplied as centrifugal (GZ) and continuous (GC) castings as well as foundry castings, so strips and rails can be cut from continuously cast bar of the same alloy as the cast inlays. The Copper Development Association warns that not all copper alloys are made in every product form, so colour-matched pieces otherwise need different alloys.
chosenBecause.source: Keskipakovalu Oy data sheet CuSn10-C (GZ and GC properties), https://www.keskipakovalu.fi/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/Data-sheet__TP10-Eng.pdf ; Copper Development Association, 'Copper Brass Bronze Design Handbook: Architectural Applications' (A4039), 'Color Matching', p. 12, https://www.copper.org/publications/pub_list/pdf/A4039-ArchitecturalApplications.pdf

chosenBecause.text: Lead-free: lead is limited to 1.0 wt% (no lead addition), which matters for rails and strips that hands and feet touch.

formation.how: Copper is melted and the tin added; the melt is poured into moulds. Statuary and inlay pieces are cast by the lost-wax (investment) process or in sand; bar, flats and hollow bar are cast continuously and then machined. Cast pieces are fettled (sprues and runners cut away) and chased (flaws removed, detail re-cut), then finished by one of the workings.

f0.derivation: value: CIELAB interpolated linearly in tin between CuSn9.5 and CuSn11 to 10 wt% Sn, (88.7, 7.17, 19.57); converted to XYZ with the D65 2-degree white and to linear Rec.709. The paper does not state its illuminant and observer; a 10-degree white gives [0.959, 0.694, 0.482]. Corrected: the 2-degree colour multiplied channel by channel by the ratio between copper's Fresnel F0 from Johnson and Christy's n,k ([0.931, 0.623, 0.522]) and copper's colour from the same instrument ([1.031, 0.645, 0.525]), giving [0.868, 0.669, 0.488]: the integrating sphere adds a few per cent of diffuse light from polishing marks. min and max are the channel-by-channel envelope of the 2-degree value, the 10-degree value and the corrected value. The true normal-incidence reflectance lies in the range.

photograph: Bright tin bronze is a warm golden metal: less red than copper, less yellow than brass.
Bare bronze indoors darkens to golden brown and then brown unless it is waxed or lacquered; it never turns green indoors.
The founder's statuary patina is a deep brown, near black in hollows, with a soft waxy sheen and bright metal on relieved high points.
A brushed strip shows fine parallel lines along its length, and its highlight is drawn out across them.
Where feet or hands pass, a strip, a rail or the dial's inlay is bright and glossy; its edges and recesses stay brown.
Green on bronze means rain, dew or salt: the outdoor patina.

unverified.reason: No measured n,k exists for Cu-Sn bronze in the sources found (refractiveindex.info holds none). This edge tint (Fresnel at 82 degrees, linear Rec.709, D65) is computed from the nearest measured copper alloy by colour, Cu85Zn15 (M. R. Querry, 'Optical constants', Contractor Report CRDC-CR-85034 (1985), https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/ADA158623 , via refractiveindex.info-database other/alloys/Cu-Zn, Querry-Cu85Zn15). It is a proxy, not a measurement of this alloy.
No handbook row for bronze or solid copper-alloy surfaces was read.
No measured shoe-on-bronze friction was found.
